title: Lesson 9: Church Planting, Missions, and Ministry Partners
description: Priscilla and Aquila had day jobs, an open home, and friends in God's mission. You will see that you were never meant to do ministry alone, and find your place with your church, ministry partners in your city, new churches, and the nations.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned how to disciple others, pouring into a few who will teach others also (2 Timothy 2:2). That is how the mission grows, one life at a time. Back in Lesson 1, you drew a personal ministry map from Acts 1:8. Now you will see who is on that map with you.

blocks.title: The Tentmakers
blocks.text:
Priscilla and Aquila were a married couple who made tents for a living. When the emperor Claudius forced the Jews out of Rome, they lost their home and moved to Corinth (Acts 18:2). There they met a traveling church planter named Paul, and "because he was of the same trade he stayed with them and worked, for they were tentmakers by trade" (Acts 18:3). They worked side by side all week, and every Sabbath Paul reasoned about Jesus in the synagogue (Acts 18:4).

When opposition rose, the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: "Do not be afraid, but go on speaking and do not be silent, for I am with you... for I have many in this city who are my people" (Acts 18:9-10). God was already at work in Corinth before any of them arrived, and a church was born.

Later the couple moved with Paul to Ephesus (Acts 18:18-19). When a gifted young preacher named Apollos came to town knowing only part of the story, they did not criticize him from a distance. They took him aside and "explained to him the way of God more accurately" (Acts 18:26), and Apollos went on to greatly help the believers in Greece (Acts 18:27). In Ephesus and later back in Rome, a church met in their home (1 Corinthians 16:19; Romans 16:5).

Years later Paul wrote, "Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who risked their necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks but all the churches of the Gentiles give thanks as well" (Romans 16:3-4). They never preached a famous sermon. They had a trade, an open door, and a willingness to go with others wherever God was working.

This is how God has always spread His church: not through a few superstars, but through ordinary people working together. Priscilla and Aquila did not have to choose between their day job and God's mission. Their workshop, their table, and their friendships all became part of it.
9.1 - Priscilla and Aquila had a trade, an open home, and friends in the mission. What has God put in your hands right now that He could use, and who could you use it with?
Your Mission Map

Jesus sent His followers to be His witnesses "in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth" (Acts 1:8). For you, that mission moves out in four circles: your church, your city, new churches, and the nations. You never join any of them alone.
Your Church and Your City

Your local church is home base. It is where you are known, fed, corrected, and sent, and it is God's main plan for reaching the world. But no single church can reach every corner of a city. That is where ministry partners come in. Campus ministries, pregnancy resource centers, food pantries, refugee ministries, sports ministries, and prison ministries gather like-minded believers to come alongside local churches and reach people a church might not reach on its own.
I thank my God in all my remembrance of you, always in every prayer of mine for all of you making my prayer with joy, because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.

A good partner ministry loves Jesus, holds to the gospel, and sends you back to your church stronger, not away from it. It can be a great place to find your personal ministry, working shoulder to shoulder with others who love God, love your city, and love people who are far from Him. Talk with your pastor before you jump in, and let your church family know where you serve so they can pray for you.

9.2 - Which people in Kansas City break your heart: students, the poor, refugees, moms facing a hard pregnancy, people in prison, or someone else? Who is already serving them that you could join instead of starting alone?
Churches That Plant Churches
The church in Antioch did something costly. While they were worshiping, the Holy Spirit asked them to give away two of their best leaders.

While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." Then after fasting and praying they laid their hands on them and sent them off.

Much of the New Testament is the story of churches planting churches. Tim Keller put it strongly: "The vigorous, continual planting of new congregations is the single most crucial strategy for (1) the numerical growth of the body of Christ in a city and (2) the continual corporate renewal and revival of the existing churches in a city." New churches reach new people, and they keep older churches from getting comfortable.

Neighborhood Church was itself a church plant, started in 2015 by a small team who prayed, threw neighborhood parties, and served a local elementary school. Since then NC has sent out NC Olathe in 2019 and The Way Church KC in 2022, and our dream is simple: Neighborhood Churches that start Neighborhood Churches. We partner with the Send Network, the church planting arm of the North American Mission Board, to help plant healthy churches across Kansas City. Think of an aspen grove. It looks like many separate trees, but underneath they share one root system. There is one church in Kansas City, and every faithful congregation grows from the same root.

You can be part of this without moving across town. You can pray for new churches and their planters by name. You can give to help a new church get started. You can serve on a launch team or at a new church's outreach. And some of you may hear God calling you to go with a team that starts a church in a neighborhood that needs one.
9.3 - Pray, give, serve, or go: which one is God stirring in you when it comes to church planting? What makes you hesitate?
To the Nations
God's mission does not stop at the city limits. One day His throne will be surrounded by worshipers from every people on earth.

After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.

John Piper wrote, "Missions is not the ultimate goal of the church. Worship is. Missions exists because worship doesn't." Thousands of people groups still have little or no access to the gospel. Southern Baptist churches like ours send missionaries together through the Cooperative Program, the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering for international missions, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering for church planting in North America. You can pray for a people group by name, give generously, go on a short-term trip, and welcome the nations already living in Kansas City, like refugee families and international students.

9.4 - Missions exists because worship doesn't. Where is worship missing that God may want you to care about: a people group, a missionary you could pray for, or a family from another country near you?

This can feel like a lot. You are not the Savior of Kansas City or the world. Jesus is, and He has already done the work that saves. You get to join Him, and you never do it alone. Like Priscilla and Aquila, you just take the next faithful step with the people God has put beside you.
Lesson 9 Review

You were never meant to do ministry alone. Priscilla and Aquila used their trade, their home, and their friendships to help plant churches in three cities, and all the churches gave thanks for them. Your mission map moves out from your church to ministry partners in your city, to new churches, and to the nations, and in every circle you can pray, give, serve, or go. In the next lesson, you will put it all together, discover how God has shaped you to serve, and find your place on a team at Neighborhood Church.
